#### 19. Management Statements
- **Vision & Strategy:** To be a top-quartile underwriter of catastrophe-exposed property insurance, focusing on low-rise commercial property insurance in Florida.
- Re-underwrites and inspects each property every three years to maintain verified data quality and insurance-to-value integrity.
- Focuses on managing PML, Total Insured Value (TIV), and Average Annual Loss (AAL). Employs AI technology to assist with intake and underwriting evaluations.

#### 20. Major Events
- **Sale of Interboro Insurance Company (IIC):** Stock Purchase Agreement entered May 9, 2024 with Forza Insurance Holdings, LLC. Approved by NYDFS February 13, 2025; closed April 1, 2025. Cash proceeds of $25,679 thousand; loss on disposal was $247 thousand (net of tax), plus $1,348 thousand net realized loss on fixed maturities.
- **UPC Receivership & Divestiture:** UPC was placed into receivership with the Florida DFS on February 27, 2023, resulting in deconsolidation and a 2023 gain of $238,440 thousand.
- **Debt Rating Upgrade:** Kroll upgraded ACIC debt from BB+ to BBB- on July 21, 2025, triggering a reduction in interest rate on Senior Notes from 7.25% to 6.25% effective December 16, 2025.
- **Regulatory Market Conduct Examination:** In 2025, FLOIR conducted an examination of AmCoastal regarding Hurricane Ian claims handling; closed via Consent Order with a $400,000 fine.
- **Equity Distribution Agreement (ATM):** Entered September 2023 with Raymond James for up to 8,000,000 shares; as of Dec 31, 2025, 4,373,000 shares sold for net proceeds of $38,190 thousand.
- **Intercompany Loan Forgiveness:** During 2025, ACIC subsidiaries forgave historical borrowings totaling $111,112 thousand, reducing investment in subsidiaries by the same amount.
- **New Excess & Surplus Entity Formation:** Capital contribution of $15,000 thousand made in 2025 to form a new E&S entity (not yet operational).

---

#### 21. Risks or Warnings Explicitly Mentioned
- **Geographic & Single-State Peril Concentration:** 100% of direct written premium and TIV are concentrated in Florida; high exposure to hurricanes, tropical storms, severe convective storms, and regulatory shifts.
- **Managing General Agent Dependence:** Exclusive MGA AmRisc produces 100% of condominium revenue (97% of total commercial lines business).
- **Catastrophe & Climate Risks:** Frequency/severity of severe weather events; PML or actual losses could exceed reinsurance limits. In 2025, 0 named storms made landfall in ACIC footprint vs. 5 in 2024.
- **Reinsurance Availability and Counterparty Risk:** Heavy reliance on external reinsurance and captive Shoreline Re. Reinsurance costs represented 52.6% of gross earned premium in 2025 (57.1% in 2024).
- **Contingent Liability / Litigation:** 
  - Florida DFS filed a claim against ACIC's D&O policy limits ($40,000 thousand) alleging former UPC officers/directors wrongful acts; ACIC accrued the $1,500 thousand policy retention in 2023.
  - Quota share commission loss contingency on contracts shared with UPC.
  - AmCoastal officers/directors subject to FLOIR inquiry under § 624.4073 Fla. Stat. regarding whether they contributed to UPC insolvency.
- **Control Concentration:** Executive Chairman R. Daniel Peed beneficially controls ~28% of common stock directly, plus a voting proxy for ~6% (total ~34%); executive officers and directors control ~49%.
- **Holding Company Limitations:** Ability of ACIC to service debt ($150,000 thousand) and pay dividends depends on dividends from AmCoastal, subject to Florida statutory limits.
